Each contrast is tested on the per-trial paired difference d = A - B (pairs matched on session x trial_idx; in a vs-zero test d is the value itself), NaN dropped, with a linear mixed model d ~ 1 + (1 | session) (session ids are unique across the two patients), fitted by REML in statsmodels MixedLM (optimizers lbfgs, powell and cg; of the fits that converge with a finite intercept SE and log-likelihood, the one with the largest log-likelihood is kept): the fixed intercept is the mean difference and the session random intercept accounts for trials within a session being correlated. Per-patient rows fit the same model to that patient's trials (4 and 5 sessions). Its Wald p is p_used for every contrast; Shapiro-Wilk on the residuals and the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p are reported in the Source Data only. Stars *** / ** / * / ns at 0.001 / 0.01 / 0.05 on p_fdr_bh, Benjamini-Hochberg over the seven displacement tests. Boxes, lines and in-figure numbers show medians, descriptively.

ONLY THE FOUR VS-ZERO STARS ARE DRAWN, one per axes, beside that condition's median endpoint; the three between-condition tests are reported here and in the caption only, with no bracket in the panel. Benjamini-Hochberg correction across these seven displacement tests: each drawn star is set on that row's p_fdr_bh (stats column star_drawn), the same values as 03_figures/results_statistics.py item 15 (family F15-displacement); the stats column star keeps the uncorrected star of p_used. The two nulls are re-runs of the same trials and the vs-zero tests re-use the same endpoints, so the seven tests are NOT independent. The Decoded condition holds both patients (P1 68 + P2 62 = 130 trials) but only two people; the session random intercept absorbs the within-session correlation of trials, but with two patients these remain TRIAL-level tests, not population-level ones.
